rv.q: Not to be missed, this raw 'Hayward.' Bring your seatbelt.
The World Premiere of Hayward is a remarkable example of how art can bring grief, anger, imperfection, and family to the stage.
“Hayward” is fresh, compelling and well worth watching.
A darkly humorous tale that wounds the heart, Hayward is a one-way cruise through the underworld of one family’s demons.
Walker’s play, which she says was inspired by Shakespeare’s Hamlet and Sophocles’ Electra , is an electric story of family life and family tragedy.
With its memorable characters, dark humor, and committed performances, Hayward offers a lively and often moving portrait of a family trying to find its way through grief.
Hayward is a spectacular production, grounded in honesty, with humor woven into the difficult moments.
This play, smoothly directed by AmBer Montgomery on a remarkable set designed by Sydney Lynne, is a chilling look at a family and the connections between its members.

cn.t: Walker's world premiere earns praise as a gripping modern family tragedy that blends Shakespearean elements with raw explorations of grief, secrets, and Black family dynamics, though its intense content demands strong audience warnings.
